title: Inbound webhooks
description: Route signed GitHub events to an agent or a schedule.

sections.title: How webhooks work
paragraphs: An inbound webhook turns a GitHub event into work. You choose which events and actions to accept and which payload fields to pass on, and whether they go to an agent or start a schedule. Create webhooks in the office settings; Bureau shows the delivery URL and the signing secret.

sections.title: Delivery URL and signature
paragraphs: Deliveries go to POST /hooks/github/{id} on the office’s public URL. Each request must carry X-Hub-Signature-256 with the HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body using the webhook secret, plus X-GitHub-Delivery and X-GitHub-Event. GitHub sends all three when you paste the URL and secret into a repository webhook.

sections.title: Making the office reachable
paragraphs: GitHub must reach the delivery URL, so the office needs a public URL such as Tailscale Funnel or your own domain. While external access is off, deliveries from outside the server machine are refused.
